title: Files, JSON, Async, and a Progress Tracker
summary: Combine domain models, collections, JSON serialization, file I/O, async/await, cancellation, and tests in a persistent tracker.
learningObjectives: Explain and apply Files, JSON, Async, and a Progress Tracker
Use compiler and runtime evidence to test the contract
prerequisiteConcepts: Ability to create and save a text file

sections.heading: Core model
sections.content: `using` and `await using` ensure disposable resources are released. High-level file APIs simplify small text operations, while streams suit larger or incremental data. Treat JSON as untrusted: deserialization can produce null or domain-invalid values, so validate before accepting state. `async` methods usually return `Task` or `Task<T>` and should be awaited; `async void` is reserved for event handlers. Pass cancellation tokens through cancellable operations. Keep I/O at the boundary and domain calculations synchronous and testable.
